newsitem.title: CHILE: Hyundai near Chile refinery decision.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai near Chile refinery decision.

text.p: South Korean industrial giant Hyundai is close to a decision on building a copper smelter and refinery in Chile which would involve an investment of between $300 million and $600 million, said a company official.
"The decision should certainly be taken within the next two months," Jaime Miranda, commercial manager for Hyundai's Chilean division, told Reuters.
Company officials were still studying a report on the scheme prepared in March by Chilean mining trade group Sonami, he said.
Hyundai is looking to build a complex with a production capacity of 400,000 tonnes of copper cathodes a year.

Industry officials said the study advised the South Korean firm that it would have no problem in finding customers for the smelter as a result of the strong growth expected in Chilean concentrate production in coming years.
The report did not recommend one specific site, although most of Chile's concentrate producers are clustered in the northern Second Region near the port of Antofagasta, said Miranda.
"Hyundai has to study all possible sites in terms of access, labour and environmental impact. Each alternative has its cost and this is being analyzed," he said.
Hyundai is one of several companies pushing for a share in Chile's booming copper smelting and refining industry.
Chilean power giant Endesa and Finland's Outokumpu Oy are studying building a $800 million smelting and refining complex.
Local refinery Refimet, fresh from one expansion, plans to boost output to handle 680,000 tonnes of concentrates a year from 450,000 tonnes now.
Chile, already the world's largest copper producer, expects copper production to climb to 4.7 million tonnes by 2000 from 2.5 million tonnes last year.
